title: Safe-Sim: Safety-Critical Closed-Loop Traffic Simulation with Diffusion-Controllable Adversaries

control_signal.value: Adversarial agent aggressiveness (e.g. TTC cost weight) and collision type via trajectory proposals; partial diffusion ratio gamma trades user control against data distribution.

control_mechanism.value: Test-time gradient guidance of denoising with adversarial and regularization objectives; partial diffusion starts denoising from noised rule-based trajectory proposals at step k_p = gamma * K.

base_model.value: Diffusion model following CTG: ResNet scene encoder, UNet-like 1D temporal convolutions, K = 100 diffusion steps; best sample chosen by lowest guidance cost.

datasets.value: Trained on nuScenes train split; evaluated on nuScenes validation and nuPlan mini validation (no fine-tuning); vehicle-to-vehicle interactions.

metrics.value: Realism via Wasserstein distance of acceleration and jerk histograms; collision rate, adversary and other off-road, collision relative speed, TTC cost, collision diversity variances, simulation time.

controllability_evidence.value: TTC cost weight 0.0/1.0/2.0 gives collision rate 48.2/53.6/60.7 %. Partial diffusion raises collision-point variance from 1.62 m to 5.44 m in the ablation.

stated_limitations.value: Adversary sometimes collides with non-adversarial agents before reaching ego, and some collisions are not the ego planner's fault.

notes: Realism score worsens slightly as TTC weight rises (0.76 to 0.81, lower is better). Compared against STRIVE and DiffScene.
